title: improv·artist · elemental (Olafur Eliasson)
mutation_directive: improv artist: elemental via Olafur Eliasson

improv_extras.practice: weather as art; light, water, ice, fog; the room becomes the medium

v1.feedback: Strong concept-to-form connection — the staggered sublimation cycle keeps Lucy readable while selling impermanence, and the warm-sun-behind-ice palette is genuinely Eliasson. Two refinements: the ambient frost motes (2800) and ground shimmer (1200) together risk diluting visual focus from the figure; halve mote count or dim them further so Lucy commands the frame. Second, the sublimation drift vector (3.8 units upward) combined with the 0.32-cycle detach window means ~30% of particles are always significantly displaced — tighten detachDur to cycle*0.22 or reduce drift magnitude to 2.4 so the statue silhouette reads solid for a longer fraction of each cycle, making the moments of dissolution more precious by contrast.

v2.feedback: Strong concept-to-form link — Lucy as Eliasson ice-watch is legible and the sublimation cycle reads as impermanence. Tighten DETACH_FRAC to ~0.12 so dissolution moments feel rarer and more precious; currently 22% detached time dilutes the 'solid most of the time' intent. The fixed camera works but a single slow lateral drift (0.001/frame over 60s, then stop) would let the warm amber edge-light sweep across the marble surface and reveal depth. Consider adding faint normal-based rim lighting in the vertex shader so the statue's curvature reads even when particles are fully attached — right now the radial-approximate sun-facing loses anatomical detail in the torso.
